[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility carries the QTS Santa Clara name within Silicon Valley, one of the historic technology and semiconductor manufacturing hubs of the San Francisco Bay Area. QTS company history describes a December 2007 transaction adding about 120,000 square feet of data center and office technology space in Silicon Valley, which is the most likely origin point for operator presence in this market, though available Wikipedia coverage of QTS does not name Santa Clara specifically or describe this exact building. QTS separately expanded into the broader Bay Area in January 2013 by acquiring Herakles LLC and its roughly 92,000 square foot data center in San Francisco, a related but distinct facility. QTS was founded in 2003 by Chad Williams and is headquartered in Overland Park, Kansas. Blackstone completed an approximately 10 billion dollar acquisition of QTS Realty Trust on August 31, 2021 at 78 dollars per share through Blackstone Infrastructure Partners and BREIT, after which QTS continued operating under its own brand as a private company. No independently confirmed street address, building history, square footage, or power capacity specific to this Santa Clara building was located this session.

reading.body:
QTS Santa Clara 1 in Santa Clara, California, publishes 7.5 MW of IT capacity, operated by Quality Technology Services.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 750 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 188 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

QTS Santa Clara 1 holds 1 published certification: LEED (a specific compliance or security standard). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

California has 22 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 10 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 356 MW. QTS Santa Clara 1 contributes 7.5 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
